findings.source_quote: ἀνακιρνάμενοι γὰρ ταῖς ψυχαῖς, ὅπως τις τῆς αὐτοῦ σωτηρίας ἀμελήσῃ, ἐνθυμήσεις πρὸς ἃ βούλονται ὑποβάλλουσιν εἰς τὸν ἑκάστου νοῦν.
findings.english_quote: For by blending themselves with souls, the demons suggest to each person’s mind thoughts directed toward whatever they wish, so that the person neglects their own salvation.
findings.issue: All the meaning is represented, but the purpose clause has been moved from between the blending and the suggestion of thoughts to the sentence’s end. This does not satisfy the express requirement to preserve clause order.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the purpose clause before the suggestion of thoughts, for example: “For the demons, blending themselves with souls so that a person may neglect their own salvation, suggest to each person’s mind thoughts directed toward whatever they wish.” This replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ εἰς τέλος κολασθησομένας καθιστᾶσιν τῶν ἀνακεκραμένων τὰς ἠπατημένας αὐτοῖς ψυχάς, ὡς ἔφαμεν, εἰς τὸ καθάρσιον χωρήσαντες πῦρ.
findings.english_quote: And, having entered the purifying fire, as we said, they bring it about that the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them will be punished to the end.
findings.issue: The draft moves both the fire-entry clause and “as we said” ahead of the punishment statement. The Greek places the punishment statement first, followed by “as we said” and then the fire-entry clause. Besides violating the required clause order, the rearrangement changes the apparent attachment of the retrospective remark. Taking χωρήσαντες with the demons is defensible and already explained; that interpretation is not itself a block.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the punishment statement first and the fire-entry clause last. One candidate retaining the draft’s subject interpretation is: “And they bring it about that the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them will be punished to the end, as we said, after they—the demons—have entered the purifying fire.” Retain the existing subject-ambiguity note and submit the replacement for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τῶν ἀνακεκραμένων τὰς ἠπατημένας αὐτοῖς ψυχάς
findings.english_quote: the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them
findings.issue: The English assigns αὐτοῖς to the mingling, but its position also naturally supports attachment to the perfect passive participle ἠπατημένας: “the souls deceived by them.” The longer-distance attachment adopted by the draft is defensible, particularly in light of the preceding discussion of blending with souls, but this material attachment alternative and the reason for choosing between them are not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining that the main text takes αὐτοῖς with ἀνακεκραμένων, supported by the blending described in 9.11, while an alternative is “the souls deceived by them, belonging to those who have been mingled.” No correction to the printed Greek is required. Any resulting English revision must receive fresh review.
